title: Cliona Francis Noronha vs Manuel John D Costa on 10 April, 2026

paragraphs.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
 CIVIL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION


 TRANSFER PETITION(S)(CIVIL) NO(S).2770/2024


 CLIONA FRANCIS NORONHA PETITIONER(S)

 VERSUS

 MANUEL JOHN D COSTA RESPONDENT(S)


 O R D E R

This Transfer Petition has been filed by the petitioner

 who is the wife of the respondent seeking the following

 prayer:

“(a) Transfer the Divorce Petition filed by the
 respondent/husband under Section 10(1)(x) of
 Indian Divorce Act, 1869 being S.M.P.No.9 of 2024
 titled as “Mr. Manuel John D’Costa Vs. Mrs.
 Cliona Francis Noronha”, pending before the Ld.
 District Judge-I & Additional Sessions Judge,
 Palghar at District Palghar, Maharashtra to the
 Family Court, Bangalore, Karnataka; and

(b) Pass such other or further order or orders as
 this Hon’ble Court may deem fit and proper on the
 facts and in the circumstances of the case, in
 favour of the petitioner and against the
 respondent.”

2. During the pendency of the Transfer Petition, the

 respondent-husband filed an application under Article 142 of
Signature Not Verified
 the Constitution of India seeking dissolution of the marriage

 by a decree of divorce by mutual consent under Section 10A of

 1
the Divorce Act, 1869 . The parties have explored the

possibility of a settlement pursuant to the application filed

by the respondent herein.

3. Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner

submitted that pursuant to the order dated 09.12.2025 passed

by this Court the petitioner is ready and willing to accept a

sum of Rs.40 lakhs in full and final settlement of all her

claims against the respondent herein by way of permanent

alimony in the event this Court is to allow the application

filed by the respondent herein under Article 142 of the

Constitution of India seeking dissolution of the marriage by

a decree of divorce by mutual consent.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent submitted that

pursuant to the aforesaid order dated 09.12.2025, a sum of

Rs.20 lakhs + 19 lakhs has been deposited with the Registry

of this Court and a sum of Rs.one lakh lying in a fixed

deposit has been withdrawn by the petitioner herein. Thus,

the petitioner may be paid the sum of Rs.40 lakhs towards

alimony in respect of all the claims made by the petitioner

herein as against the respondent. Learned counsel for the

respondent therefore submitted that the application filed by

the respondent herein under Article 142 of the Constitution

of India may be allowed since the petitioner is agreeable for

such a relief.

5. Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner also

submitted that the petitioner is agreeable for the

dissolution of the marriage and the application filed by the

respondent herein may be allowed.

6. In the above backdrop we have taken on record, the

application filed by the respondent herein.
7. We have considered the arguments advanced at the bar.

8. The parties are also present before this Court through

video conferencing facility.

9. When we queried the parties, they submitted that they

have indeed arrived at a settlement. They have decided to

partways and seek dissolution of marriage that took place on

05.04.2021 by a decree of divorce by mutual consent; that the

parties have arrived at such a decision on their own free

volition without there being any coercion or undue influence

from any side. The petitioner-wife also submitted that the

application filed by the respondent-husband under Article 142 

of the Constitution of India may be allowed and she has no

objection for the dissolution of marriage by a decree of

divorce by mutual consent.

10. We have perused the application filed by the respondent

herein.

11. We have also perused the order dated 09.12.2025. For

ease of reference the said order reads as under:

“We have heard learned counsel for the
 petitioner and learned counsel for the
 respondent, at length, in the presence of the
 parties who have appeared through video
 conferencing facility.

The petitioner is agreeable to receive a
 sum of Rupees forty lakhs in full and final
 settlement of all her claims as against the
 respondent by way of permanent alimony in the
 event this Court is to allow the application
 filed by the respondent herein under Article
 142 of the Constitution seeking dissolution of
 the marriage by a decree of divorce by mutual
 consent.

Learned counsel for the respondent
 submitted that initially a sum of Rupees twenty
 lakhs would be deposited before this Court if
 some time is granted.

Hence, the said amount of Rupees twenty
 lakhs may be deposited before this Court within
 a period of one week from today. On such
 deposit, the Registry of this Court shall
 invest the same in a fixed deposit for an
 initial period upto 31.03.2026.

The balance amount of Rupees nineteen Lakhs
 (excluding Rupees One Lakh, which is stated to
 be in a fixed deposit in the name of the
 petitioner), shall be deposited on or before
 31.03.2026.

On such deposit being made, list this
 matter before this Court on 06.04.2026 for
 consideration of the application filed under
 Article 142 of the Constitution of India and
 for passing orders thereon.

In view of the possible settlement between
 the parties in the aforesaid terms, there shall
 be stay of further proceedings in
 Crl.Misc.No.115 of 2025 pending on the file of
 the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class
 (Traffic Court-V), Bengaluru until further
 4
 orders.

However, the pendency of the proceedings
 between the parties would not come in the way
 of the parties deciding to reside together.”

12. It is also noted that a sum of Rs.39 lakhs has been

deposited by the respondent with the Registry of this Court.

13. Learned counsel for the respondent also submitted the

Domestic Violence Case i.e., Crl. Misc. No. 115 of 2025

pending on the file of Judicial Magistrate, First Class,

Traffic Court, Bengaluru, may also be quashed. Learned senior

counsel for the petitioner also has no objection to be

quashed. There is no other proceeding pending between the

parties.

14. In the circumstances, we take note of the submissions

made at the bar and the statements made by the respective

parties.

15. Consequently, we allow the application filed by the

respondent under Article 142 of the constitution of India.

The marriage solemnised between the parties on 05.04.2021 at

Maharashtra stands dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual

consent under Section 10A of the Divorce Act, 1869, stands

dissolved.

16. The Registry is directed to transmit a sum of Rs.39

lakhs to the petitioner herein with accrued interest, if any,

to account of the petitioner herein through RTGS/IMPS viz.,

Account Number; 0444101019074, Canara Bank, Account Holder

Name: Cliona C.Noronha, IFSC Code: CNRB0000411; Branch

Address: #628, 629, III Block, Rajajinagar.

17. In view of the aforesaid order, it is expected that the

parties shall not litigate against each other.
18. Registry to draw up a decree in the aforesaid terms.

19. Transfer Petition is accordingly allowed in the

aforesaid terms.
